import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import numpy as np
fig, ax = plt.subplots(1, figsize=(5, 5))
ax.axis('on')
ax.set_title('Logo or a Data Visualization?', fontdict={'fontsize': '15', 'fontweight' : '10'})

N = 550
r0 = 0.6
x = 0.9 * np.random.rand(N)
y = 0.9 * np.random.rand(N)
area = (20 * np.random.rand(N))**2  # 0 to 10 point radii
c = np.sqrt(area)
r = np.sqrt(x ** 2 + y ** 2)
area1 = np.ma.masked_where(r < r0, area)
area2 = np.ma.masked_where(r >= r0, area)
plt.scatter(x, y, s=area1, marker='^', c=c)
plt.scatter(x, y, s=area2, marker='o', c=c)

plt.show()

import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import numpy as np
import seaborn as sns

# create a colorblind-friendly color palette
palette = sns.color_palette("colorblind")

fig, ax = plt.subplots(1, figsize=(8, 6))
ax.axis('on')
ax.set_title('Logo or a Data Visualization?', fontdict={'fontsize': '20', 'fontweight' : 'bold'})

N = 550
r0 = 0.6
x = 0.9 * np.random.rand(N)
y = 0.9 * np.random.rand(N)
area = (20 * np.random.rand(N))**2  # 0 to 10 point radii
c = np.sqrt(area)

# plot the first scatter plot with marker '^' and masked area
r = np.sqrt(x ** 2 + y ** 2)
area1 = np.ma.masked_where(r < r0, area)
ax.scatter(x, y, s=area1, marker='^', c=palette[0], alpha=0.8, edgecolors='none')

# plot the second scatter plot with marker 'o' and masked area
area2 = np.ma.masked_where(r >= r0, area)
ax.scatter(x, y, s=area2, marker='o', c=palette[1], alpha=0.8, edgecolors='none')

# add a legend
ax.legend(['Scatter plot 1', 'Scatter plot 2'], loc='upper right')

# add x and y axis labels
ax.set_xlabel('X-axis label', fontsize=14)
ax.set_ylabel('Y-axis label', fontsize=14)

# add grid lines
ax.grid(True, alpha=0.5)

# add a text box with additional information
textstr = 'Additional information\n\nElement 1\nElement 2\nElement 3'
props = dict(boxstyle='round', facecolor='white', alpha=0.5)
ax.text(0.05, 0.95, textstr, transform=ax.transAxes, fontsize=12, verticalalignment='top', bbox=props)

plt.show()

import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import numpy as np
import seaborn as sns

# create a colorblind-friendly color palette
palette = sns.color_palette("colorblind")

fig, ax = plt.subplots(1, figsize=(8, 6))
ax.axis('on')
ax.set_title('My Blog Logo', fontdict={'fontsize': '20', 'fontweight' : 'bold'})

N = 550
r0 = 0.6
x = 0.9 * np.random.rand(N)
y = 0.9 * np.random.rand(N)
area = (20 * np.random.rand(N))**2  # 0 to 10 point radii
c = np.sqrt(area)

# plot the first scatter plot with marker '^' and masked area
r = np.sqrt(x ** 2 + y ** 2)
area1 = np.ma.masked_where(r < r0, area)
ax.scatter(x, y, s=area1, marker='^', c=palette[0], alpha=0.8, edgecolors='none')

# plot the second scatter plot with marker 'o' and masked area
area2 = np.ma.masked_where(r >= r0, area)
ax.scatter(x, y, s=area2, marker='o', c=palette[1], alpha=0.8, edgecolors='none')

# add x and y axis labels with witty names and values
ax.set_xlabel('Happiness after reading (in smiles)', fontsize=14)
ax.set_ylabel('Productivity after reading(in coffee cups)', fontsize=14)

# add text on top of the scatter plot with the brand name
ax.text(0.5, 1.1, 'My Amazing Blog', transform=ax.transAxes, ha='center', va='center', fontsize=18)

ax.legend(['My Blog Posts', 'Standard Blog Posts'], loc='upper right')

# change the background color of the plot to yellow
ax.set_facecolor('#FFFFCC')

# add a border to the plot
ax.spines['top'].set_visible(False)
ax.spines['right'].set_visible(False)
ax.spines['bottom'].set_linewidth(2)
ax.spines['bottom'].set_color('#1a1a1a')
ax.spines['left'].set_linewidth(2)
ax.spines['left'].set_color('#1a1a1a')

# add grid lines
ax.grid(True, alpha=0.5)

plt.show()

import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import numpy as np
import seaborn as sns

# create a colorblind-friendly color palette
palette = sns.color_palette("colorblind")

fig, ax = plt.subplots(1, figsize=(8, 6))
ax.axis('on')
ax.set_title('My Blog Logo', fontdict={'fontsize': '20', 'fontweight' : 'bold'})

N = 550
r0 = 0.6
x = 0.9 * np.random.rand(N)
y = 0.9 * np.random.rand(N)
area = (20 * np.random.rand(N))**2  # 0 to 10 point radii
c = np.sqrt(area)

# plot the first scatter plot with marker 'o' and masked area
r = np.sqrt(x ** 2 + (y-0.5) ** 2)
area1 = np.ma.masked_where(r > r0, area)
ax.scatter(x, y, s=area1, marker='o', c=palette[1], alpha=0.8, edgecolors='none')

# plot the second scatter plot with marker '^' and masked area
area2 = np.ma.masked_where(r <= r0, area)
ax.scatter(x, y, s=area2, marker='^', c=palette[0], alpha=0.8, edgecolors='none')

# add x and y axis labels with witty names and values
ax.set_xlabel('Blog Power: How much my blog can change the world (in megawatts)', fontsize=14)
ax.set_ylabel('Blog Joy: How happy my blog makes people (in smileys)', fontsize=14)

# add text on top of the scatter plot with the brand name
ax.text(0.5, 1.1, 'My Awesome Blog', transform=ax.transAxes, ha='center', va='center', fontsize=18)

# change the background color of the plot to yellow
ax.set_facecolor('#FFFFCC')

# add a border to the plot
ax.spines['top'].set_visible(False)
ax.spines['right'].set_visible(False)
ax.spines['bottom'].set_linewidth(2)
ax.spines['bottom'].set_color('#1a1a1a')
ax.spines['left'].set_linewidth(2)

import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import numpy as np



# Define the data for the bar chart
my_blog_scores = [8, 9, 7, 10, 6]
standard_blog_scores = [6, 7, 5, 8, 4]
labels = ['Blog Pizazz', 'Blog Engagement', 'Blog Creativity', 'Blog Growth', 'Blog Community']

# Create the bar chart
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(10, 10))
ax.set_facecolor('#E5E5E5')
ax.spines['top'].set_visible(False)
ax.spines['right'].set_visible(False)
ax.spines['bottom'].set_color('#666666')
ax.spines['left'].set_color('#666666')
ax.tick_params(axis='both', which='major', colors='#666666', labelsize=10)
ax.set_axisbelow(True)
ax.yaxis.grid(True, linestyle='-', linewidth=0.5, color='#CCCCCC')

x = np.arange(len(labels))
width = 0.35
rects1 = ax.bar(x - width/2, my_blog_scores, width, label='My Blog', color='#FFBF69')
rects2 = ax.bar(x + width/2, standard_blog_scores, width, label='Standard Blog', color='#59A5D8')

# Add some witty and creative axis labels
ax.set_xlabel('Blog Superpowers', fontsize=12, fontweight='bold', color='#333333')
ax.set_ylabel('Score (out of 10)', fontsize=12, fontweight='bold', color='#333333')
ax.set_xticks(x)
ax.set_xticklabels(labels, fontsize=10, fontweight='bold', color='#333333')
ax.set_title('How My Blog is Better Than Standard Blogs', fontsize=14, fontweight='bold', color='#333333')


ax.set_facecolor('#FFFFCC')
# Add a legend and show the plot
ax.legend(loc='lower right', frameon=False, fontsize=10)
plt.show()

import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import numpy as np

# Define the data for the box plot
my_scores = [8, 9, 7, 10, 6, 9, 7, 8, 6, 9]
your_scores = [4, 5, 6, 7, 8, 5, 6, 7, 8, 6]
labels = ['My Blog', 'Your Blog']

# Create the box plot
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(6, 5))
ax.set_facecolor('#E5E5E5')
ax.spines['top'].set_visible(False)
ax.spines['right'].set_visible(False)
ax.spines['bottom'].set_color('#666666')
ax.spines['left'].set_color('#666666')
ax.tick_params(axis='both', which='major', colors='#666666', labelsize=10)
ax.set_axisbelow(True)
ax.yaxis.grid(True, linestyle='-', linewidth=0.5, color='#CCCCCC')

data = [my_scores, your_scores]
ax.boxplot(data, labels=labels, notch=True, widths=0.4, patch_artist=True,
           boxprops=dict(facecolor='#FFBF69', color='#666666'),
           whiskerprops=dict(color='#666666'),
           flierprops=dict(marker='o', markersize=5, markeredgecolor='#666666'),
           medianprops=dict(color='#333333'))


ax.set_facecolor('#FFFFCC')

# Add a funny and creative axis label
ax.set_ylabel('Score (out of 10) - Because Size Matters!', fontsize=12, fontweight='bold', color='#333333')
ax.set_title('My Blog vs. Your Blog - Who Has the Bigger Box?', fontsize=14, fontweight='bold', color='#333333')

plt.show()

from scipy.stats import norm

import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import numpy as np
from scipy.stats import poisson

# Define the parameters of the Poisson distribution
mu = 0.1  # Average number of rare events per day
n = 10000  # Number of days

# Create a range of values for the x-axis
x = np.arange(0, 50)

# Calculate the Poisson distribution for the given parameters
y = poisson.pmf(x, mu * n)

# Plot the Poisson distribution
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(10, 10))
ax.plot(x, y, color='#69B0FF')

# Add a witty and funny axis label
ax.set_xlabel('Number of Rare Events - Who Said They Were Common?', fontsize=12, fontweight='bold', color='#333333')
ax.set_ylabel('Probability Mass Function - Because We All Love Poisson', fontsize=12, fontweight='bold', color='#333333')
ax.set_title('Comparing Blogs - How Rare is Your Content?', fontsize=14, fontweight='bold', color='#333333')

# Add a vertical line to represent the average number of rare events in your blog
ax.axvline(x=mu * n, color='#FF7F50', linestyle='--', linewidth=2)
ax.text(mu * n + 0.5, 0.1, 'Your Blog', fontsize=12, fontweight='bold', color='#333333')

# Add a vertical line to represent the average number of rare events in other blogs
other_mu = 0.05
other_n = 1000
ax.axvline(x=other_mu * other_n, color='#20B2AA', linestyle='--', linewidth=2)
ax.text(other_mu * other_n + 0.5, 0.03, 'Other Blogs', fontsize=12, fontweight='bold', color='#333333')

plt.show()

import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

# Define data for pie charts

import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import numpy as np

# Generate random data
n = 50
x = np.random.rand(n)
y = np.random.rand(n)
z = np.random.rand(n)
s = np.random.rand(n) * 1000  # Bubble size

# Define labels for the bubble chart
labels = ['Funny', 'Witty', 'Humorous', 'Engaging']

# Define colors for the bubble chart
colors = ['#66c2a5', '#fc8d62', '#8da0cb', '#e78ac3']

# Create the figure and set the title
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(8, 8))
fig.suptitle('Comparison of My Blog with Others', fontsize=16, fontweight='bold')

# Create the bubble chart
for i in range(n):
    ax.scatter(x[i], y[i], s=s[i], c=colors[i % len(colors)], alpha=0.5, edgecolors='none')
    ax.annotate(labels[i % len(labels)], (x[i], y[i]), fontsize=10, ha='center', va='center')

# Set the x and y axis labels
ax.set_xlabel('Engagement')
ax.set_ylabel('Humor')

# Show the plot
plt.show()

import statsmodels.api as sm
import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

# Generate some random data for the independent and dependent variables
x = np.random.rand(100)
y = 2*x + np.random.rand(100)

# Create a dataframe with the independent and dependent variables
data = pd.DataFrame({'x': x, 'y': y})

# Run the OLS regression
model = sm.OLS(data['y'], sm.add_constant(data['x'])).fit()

# Print the regression summary
print(model.summary())

# Create a scatterplot of the data with the regression line
plt.scatter(x, y)
plt.plot(x, model.predict(sm.add_constant(x)), color='red')
plt.show()

import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

# Define the inputs and outputs for the AND gate
inputs = [(0, 0), (0, 1), (1, 0), (1, 1)]
outputs = [0, 0, 0, 1]

# Define a function to simulate the AND gate
def AND(x1, x2):
    w1, w2, theta = 0.5, 0.5, 0.7
    tmp = x1 * w1 + x2 * w2
    if tmp <= theta:
        return 0
    else:
        return 1

# Test the AND gate with the inputs and outputs
for i in range(len(inputs)):
    x1, x2 = inputs[i]
    y = outputs[i]
    print("Input:", (x1, x2), "| Output:", AND(x1, x2), "| Expected:", y)

# Generate a graph to visualize the AND gate
plt.scatter([0, 1, 0], [0, 0, 1], color='blue', label='0')
plt.scatter([1], [1], color='red', label='1')
plt.plot([0, 1], [0, 1], color='black', linestyle='--', label='AND')
plt.xlabel('Input 1')
plt.ylabel('Input 2')
plt.title('AND Gate')
plt.legend()
plt.show()

import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import numpy as np

# Define data for the bar chart
my_blog = [50, 60, 70, 80]
blog_a = [20, 30, 40, 50]
blog_b = [10, 15, 20, 25]
blog_c = [5, 10, 15, 20]

# Define labels for the x-axis and the stacked bars
categories = ['Fun', 'Wit', 'Humor', 'Laughs']

# Define colors for the stacked bars
colors = ['#66c2a5', '#fc8d62', '#8da0cb', '#e78ac3']

# Define hatch patterns for the stacked bars
hatches = ['*', '\\\\\\', 'o', '---']

# Create the figure and set the title
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(8, 6))
fig.suptitle("Why My Blog is Better Than Standard Blogs", fontsize=16, fontweight='bold')

# Create the stacked bars
ax.bar(categories, my_blog, color=colors, hatch=hatches[0], label='My Blog')
ax.bar(categories, blog_a, bottom=my_blog, color=colors, hatch=hatches[1], label='Blog A')
ax.bar(categories, blog_b, bottom=np.array(my_blog) + np.array(blog_a), color=colors, hatch=hatches[2], label='Blog B')
ax.bar(categories, blog_c, bottom=np.array(my_blog) + np.array(blog_a) + np.array(blog_b), color=colors, hatch=hatches[3], label='Blog C')

# Add labels to the x-axis and y-axis
ax.set_xlabel('Categories', fontsize=12, fontweight='bold')
ax.set_ylabel('Score', fontsize=12, fontweight='bold')

# Add a legend to the plot
ax.legend(loc='upper left', bbox_to_anchor=(1, 1), title='Blogs', title_fontsize=12)

# Add some witty text to the plot
ax.text(0.5, 0.5, "Because I'm funnier than\na clown on roller skates", fontsize=20, fontweight='bold', ha='center', va='center', transform=ax.transAxes)

# Show the plot
plt.show()

import plotly.graph_objs as go

# Define the nodes and links for the Sankey diagram
nodes = ["Start", "Introduction", "Body", "Conclusion", "End"]
links = [
    {"source": 0, "target": 1, "value": 1000},  # 1000 readers start reading
    {"source": 1, "target": 2, "value": 800},   # 800 readers continue to body
    {"source": 1, "target": 3, "value": 200},   # 200 readers skip to conclusion
    {"source": 2, "target": 3, "value": 500},   # 500 readers continue to conclusion
    {"source": 3, "target": 4, "value": 600},   # 600 readers reach the end
    {"source": 2, "target": 4, "value": 300},   # 300 readers drop off in the body
]

# Define the layout of the Sankey diagram
layout = go.Layout(
    title="Engagement with Blog Post",
    font=dict(size=10),
    width=800,
    height=400,
    margin=dict(l=50, r=50, b=50, t=50),
)

# Define the Sankey diagram trace
trace = go.Sankey(
    node=dict(
        pad=20,
        thickness=20,
        line=dict(width=0.5),
        label=nodes,
        color=["green", "blue", "orange", "blue", "green"]
    ),
    link=dict(
        source=[link["source"] for link in links],
        target=[link["target"] for link in links],
        value=[link["value"] for link in links],
        color="black",
    ),
)

# Plot the Sankey diagram
fig = go.Figure(data=[trace], layout=layout)
fig.show()

ax.text(0, 0.9, "Why My Blog is Like Batman and Others are Like Robin and Batgirl", fontsize=10)

# Display Sankey diagram
diagrams = sankey.finish()

import numpy as np
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

# Define data for radar chart
powers = ['Strength', 'Speed', 'Intelligence', 'Durability', 'Special Ability']
my_blog_powers = [8, 7, 9, 9, 7, 8]
blog_A_powers = [4, 5, 6, 4, 4, 2]
blog_B_powers = [6, 4, 5, 5, 5, 3]

# Define angle and power values for radar chart
angles = np.linspace(0, 2*np.pi, len(powers), endpoint=False)
angles = np.concatenate((angles,[angles[0]]))

# Plot the radar chart
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(6, 6), subplot_kw=dict(polar=True))
ax.plot(angles, my_blog_powers, color='green', linewidth=1, linestyle='solid', label='My Blog')
ax.fill(angles, my_blog_powers, alpha=0.25, color='green')
ax.plot(angles, blog_A_powers, color='red', linewidth=1, linestyle='solid', label='Blog A')
ax.fill(angles, blog_A_powers, alpha=0.25, color='red')
ax.plot(angles, blog_B_powers, color='blue', linewidth=1, linestyle='solid', label='Blog B')
ax.fill(angles, blog_B_powers, alpha=0.25, color='blue')

# Set the axis labels and ticks
ax.set_thetagrids(angles[:-1] * 180/np.pi, powers)
ax.set_theta_zero_location("N")
ax.set_theta_direction(-1)
ax.set_ylim(0, 10)
ax.set_title("Comparison of Superhero Powers: My Blog vs Other Blogs", fontsize=16, fontweight='bold')

# Add legend
plt.legend(loc='upper right', bbox_to_anchor=(1.3, 1))

# Show the plot
plt.show()

import plotly.express as px
import geopandas as gpd
import shapely.geometry
import numpy as np
import wget

# download a zipped shapefile
wget.download("https://plotly.github.io/datasets/ne_50m_rivers_lake_centerlines.zip")

# open a zipped shapefile with the zip:// pseudo-protocol
geo_df = gpd.read_file("zip://ne_50m_rivers_lake_centerlines.zip")

lats = []
lons = []
names = []

for feature, name in zip(geo_df.geometry, geo_df.name):
    if isinstance(feature, shapely.geometry.linestring.LineString):
        linestrings = [feature]
    elif isinstance(feature, shapely.geometry.multilinestring.MultiLineString):
        linestrings = feature.geoms
    else:
        continue
    for linestring in linestrings:
        x, y = linestring.xy
        lats = np.append(lats, y)
        lons = np.append(lons, x)
        names = np.append(names, [name]*len(y))
        lats = np.append(lats, None)
        lons = np.append(lons, None)
        names = np.append(names, None)

fig = px.line_mapbox(lat=lats, lon=lons, hover_name=names,
                     mapbox_style="stamen-terrain", zoom=1)
fig.show()

import plotly.graph_objects as go

import pandas as pd

url = "https://raw.githubusercontent.com/plotly/datasets/master/gapminderDataFiveYear.csv"
dataset = pd.read_csv(url)

years = ["1952", "1962", "1967", "1972", "1977", "1982", "1987", "1992", "1997", "2002",
         "2007"]

# make list of continents
continents = []
for continent in dataset["continent"]:
    if continent not in continents:
        continents.append(continent)
# make figure
fig_dict = {
    "data": [],
    "layout": {},
    "frames": []
}

# fill in most of layout
fig_dict["layout"]["xaxis"] = {"range": [30, 85], "title": "Life Expectancy"}
fig_dict["layout"]["yaxis"] = {"title": "GDP per Capita", "type": "log"}
fig_dict["layout"]["hovermode"] = "closest"
fig_dict["layout"]["updatemenus"] = [
    {
        "buttons": [
            {
                "args": [None, {"frame": {"duration": 500, "redraw": False},
                                "fromcurrent": True, "transition": {"duration": 300,
                                                                    "easing": "quadratic-in-out"}}],
                "label": "Play",
                "method": "animate"
            },
            {
                "args": [[None], {"frame": {"duration": 0, "redraw": False},
                                  "mode": "immediate",
                                  "transition": {"duration": 0}}],
                "label": "Pause",
                "method": "animate"
            }
        ],
        "direction": "left",
        "pad": {"r": 10, "t": 87},
        "showactive": False,
        "type": "buttons",
        "x": 0.1,
        "xanchor": "right",
        "y": 0,
        "yanchor": "top"
    }
]

sliders_dict = {
    "active": 0,
    "yanchor": "top",
    "xanchor": "left",
    "currentvalue": {
        "font": {"size": 20},
        "prefix": "Year:",
        "visible": True,
        "xanchor": "right"
    },
    "transition": {"duration": 300, "easing": "cubic-in-out"},
    "pad": {"b": 10, "t": 50},
    "len": 0.9,
    "x": 0.1,
    "y": 0,
    "steps": []
}

# make data
year = 1952
for continent in continents:
    dataset_by_year = dataset[dataset["year"] == year]
    dataset_by_year_and_cont = dataset_by_year[
        dataset_by_year["continent"] == continent]

    data_dict = {
        "x": list(dataset_by_year_and_cont["lifeExp"]),
        "y": list(dataset_by_year_and_cont["gdpPercap"]),
        "mode": "markers",
        "text": list(dataset_by_year_and_cont["country"]),
        "marker": {
            "sizemode": "area",
            "sizeref": 200000,
            "size": list(dataset_by_year_and_cont["pop"])
        },
        "name": continent
    }
    fig_dict["data"].append(data_dict)

# make frames
for year in years:
    frame = {"data": [], "name": str(year)}
    for continent in continents:
        dataset_by_year = dataset[dataset["year"] == int(year)]
        dataset_by_year_and_cont = dataset_by_year[
            dataset_by_year["continent"] == continent]

        data_dict = {
            "x": list(dataset_by_year_and_cont["lifeExp"]),
            "y": list(dataset_by_year_and_cont["gdpPercap"]),
            "mode": "markers",
            "text": list(dataset_by_year_and_cont["country"]),
            "marker": {
                "sizemode": "area",
                "sizeref": 200000,
                "size": list(dataset_by_year_and_cont["pop"])
            },
            "name": continent
        }
        frame["data"].append(data_dict)

    fig_dict["frames"].append(frame)
    slider_step = {"args": [
        [year],
        {"frame": {"duration": 300, "redraw": False},
         "mode": "immediate",
         "transition": {"duration": 300}}
    ],
        "label": year,
        "method": "animate"}
    sliders_dict["steps"].append(slider_step)


fig_dict["layout"]["sliders"] = [sliders_dict]

fig = go.Figure(fig_dict)

fig.show()

import plotly.graph_objects as go
import pandas as pd
df = pd.read_csv('https://raw.githubusercontent.com/plotly/datasets/master/1962_2006_walmart_store_openings.csv')
df.head()

data = []
layout = dict(
    title = 'New Walmart Stores per year 1962-2006<br>\
Source: <a href="http://www.econ.umn.edu/~holmes/data/WalMart/index.html">\
University of Minnesota</a>',
    # showlegend = False,
    autosize = False,
    width = 1000,
    height = 900,
    hovermode = False,
    legend = dict(
        x=0.7,
        y=-0.1,
        bgcolor="rgba(255, 255, 255, 0)",
        font = dict( size=11 ),
    )
)
years = df['YEAR'].unique()

for i in range(len(years)):
    geo_key = 'geo'+str(i+1) if i != 0 else 'geo'
    lons = list(df[ df['YEAR'] == years[i] ]['LON'])
    lats = list(df[ df['YEAR'] == years[i] ]['LAT'])
    # Walmart store data
    data.append(
        dict(
            type = 'scattergeo',
            showlegend=False,
            lon = lons,
            lat = lats,
            geo = geo_key,
            name = int(years[i]),
            marker = dict(
                color = "rgb(0, 0, 255)",
                opacity = 0.5
            )
        )
    )
    # Year markers
    data.append(
        dict(
            type = 'scattergeo',
            showlegend = False,
            lon = [-78],
            lat = [47],
            geo = geo_key,
            text = [years[i]],
            mode = 'text',
        )
    )
    layout[geo_key] = dict(
        scope = 'usa',
        showland = True,
        landcolor = 'rgb(229, 229, 229)',
        showcountries = False,
        domain = dict( x = [], y = [] ),
        subunitcolor = "rgb(255, 255, 255)",
    )


def draw_sparkline( domain, lataxis, lonaxis ):
    ''' Returns a sparkline layout object for geo coordinates  '''
    return dict(
        showland = False,
        showframe = False,
        showcountries = False,
        showcoastlines = False,
        domain = domain,
        lataxis = lataxis,
        lonaxis = lonaxis,
        bgcolor = 'rgba(255,200,200,0.0)'
    )

# Stores per year sparkline
layout['geo44'] = draw_sparkline({'x':[0.6,0.8], 'y':[0,0.15]}, \
                                 {'range':[-5.0, 30.0]}, {'range':[0.0, 40.0]} )
data.append(
    dict(
        type = 'scattergeo',
        mode = 'lines',
        lat = list(df.groupby(by=['YEAR']).count()['storenum']/1e1),
        lon = list(range(len(df.groupby(by=['YEAR']).count()['storenum']/1e1))),
        line = dict( color = "rgb(0, 0, 255)" ),
        name = "New stores per year<br>Peak of 178 stores per year in 1990",
        geo = 'geo44',
    )
)

# Cumulative sum sparkline
layout['geo45'] = draw_sparkline({'x':[0.8,1], 'y':[0,0.15]}, \
                                 {'range':[-5.0, 50.0]}, {'range':[0.0, 50.0]} )
data.append(
    dict(
        type = 'scattergeo',
        mode = 'lines',
        lat = list(df.groupby(by=['YEAR']).count().cumsum()['storenum']/1e2),
        lon = list(range(len(df.groupby(by=['YEAR']).count()['storenum']/1e1))),
        line = dict( color = "rgb(214, 39, 40)" ),
        name ="Cumulative sum<br>3176 stores total in 2006",
        geo = 'geo45',
    )
)

z = 0
COLS = 5
ROWS = 9
for y in reversed(range(ROWS)):
    for x in range(COLS):
        geo_key = 'geo'+str(z+1) if z != 0 else 'geo'
        layout[geo_key]['domain']['x'] = [float(x)/float(COLS), float(x+1)/float(COLS)]
        layout[geo_key]['domain']['y'] = [float(y)/float(ROWS), float(y+1)/float(ROWS)]
        z=z+1
        if z > 42:
            break

fig = go.Figure(data=data, layout=layout)
fig.update_layout(width=800)
fig.show()
